JSON: Name: locomamba_pipeline Title: End-to-end vision-driven quadrupedal locomotion using stacked Mamba selective state-space fusion with proprioceptive and depth tokens Short Hypothesis: Fusing proprioceptive state tokens and patchified depth tokens with a stacked Mamba selective state-space model inside an end-to-end PPO policy yields higher sample efficiency, greater final task return, and fewer obstacle collisions in quadrupedal locomotion than (a) the same architecture using a Transformer-based fusion or (b) policies using only proprioception or only vision, when evaluated under identical domain randomization and curricula. Related Work: Prior approaches to quadrupedal locomotion include model-based MPC and trajectory-optimization pipelines that require precise dynamics and contact modeling, and learning-based policies trained with reinforcement learning. Learning-based solutions often operate on proprioceptive inputs only (blind policies) trading foresight for simplicity, while cross-modal fusion methods add exteroceptive perception (depth or RGB) to provide look-ahead. Recurrent backbones (LSTM/GRU) provide streaming temporal aggregation but can suffer from vanishing gradients and limited long-horizon capacity. Transformer-based fusion delivers strong expressivity and global context but incurs quadratic memory and compute cost with token length, limiting spatial resolution and sequence horizon. Existing multimodal fusions also use concatenation or hierarchical decompositions that either underuse spatial structure or increase optimization complexity and error propagation. These limitations leave unresolved trade-offs between long-horizon temporal modeling, real-time latency, memory scaling, and robust cross-modal grounding for control. Abstract: We address end-to-end vision-driven quadrupedal locomotion in obstacle-rich and uneven environments by proposing a cross-modal reinforcement learning pipeline that fuses proprioceptive states and first-person depth via a stacked Mamba selective state-space model. The pipeline encodes proprioception with a compact MLP and patchifies depth images into spatial tokens with a lightweight CNN, projects both modalities to a shared token width, and scans tokens with stacked Mamba layers to produce fused features consumed by policy and value heads trained with PPO. The main contribution is the integration of a near-linear-time, input-gated selective state-space backbone for cross-modal fusion that supports long-horizon dependencies while reducing latency and memory compared to attention-based fusion. We expect the proposed pipeline to improve sample efficiency, final return, and collision avoidance under domain randomization and obstacle-density curricula, and to generalize better to unseen dynamic and rugged terrains while maintaining practical runtime and memory requirements. Experiments: Datasets and environments: Simulated quadrupedal locomotion tasks in PyBullet with three primary scenarios: (1) Thin Obstacle (flat ground with dense thin cuboid obstacles), (2) RuggedTerrain (uneven discontinuous ground up to 5 cm), (3) DynamicObstacle (thin obstacles with randomized motion during episodes). Zero-shot evaluation on two unseen environments: Rugged Unseen (distinct terrain seed distribution) and Dynamic Unseen (different obstacle motion patterns). Models and baselines: (A) LocoMamba: proprioceptive MLP + CNN patchified depth + 2-layer stacked Mamba SSM + PPO; (B) Transformer Proprio-Vision: same encoders but cross-modal Transformer fusion; (C) Mamba Vision-Only: depth tokens only with Mamba backbone; (D) Transformer Vision-Only: depth tokens with Transformer; (E) Proprio-Only: proprioceptive MLP only; (F) Proprio-Vision-Concatenate: modality projection followed by direct concatenation and MLP. Ablations: (i) token count ablation (32, 64, 256 depth tokens), (ii) number of Mamba layers (1,2,4), (iii) remove input gating in SSM, (iv) vary obstacle-density curriculum schedule (linear vs step). Training protocol: PPO with identical hyperparameters across methods (episode horizon 999, 16,384 samples/iteration, minibatch 1,024, epochs 3, γ=0.99, GAE λ=0.95), domain randomization ranges matched per run, 10 independent seeds per method. Evaluation metrics: mean episode return, progress distance along task direction (meters), collisions per episode, sample-efficiency curves (return vs environment interactions), coefficient of variation of value-loss and advantage estimates over training, throughput (samples/sec), peak and allocated GPU memory (MB), FLOPs per step. Experimental setup: train until 2M environment steps or convergence, evaluate every fixed interval on 100 episodes per seed; report mean±std across 10 seeds. Specific comparisons: (1) LocoMamba vs Transformer Proprio-Vision (primary baseline) on all metrics; (2) modality ablation: LocoMamba vs Proprio-Only and Vision-Only; (3) efficiency ablation: token-count and Mamba-layer sweeps measuring FLOPs, memory, and throughput; (4) robust generalization: zero-shot tests on Rugged Unseen and Dynamic Unseen; (5) statistical test: paired t-test on final returns between LocoMamba and best baseline (α=0.05). Risk Factors and Limitations: Technical failure modes: instability in on-policy optimization leading to high variance runs or collapse; sensitivity of selective SSM to misaligned sensor timestamps or missing depth frames causing recurrent state drift. Data and evaluation biases: simulated depth and dynamics may not capture real sensor artifacts (occlusions, motion blur, depth bias) and contact variability, leading to overestimated zero-shot performance. Scalability and compute: although Mamba scales near-linearly with token count, increasing token resolution or stacking many layers raises memory and FLOPs, possibly exceeding onboard compute for real-time control. Generalization limits: learned policies may overfit to randomized ranges and curricula and fail under out-of-distribution terrains or obstacle geometries; vision-only variants may exhibit degraded temporal anchoring without proprioception. Safety limits: collisions in real hardware carry physical risk; sim-to-real transfer requires additional robustness checks. Measurement limitations: metrics like collisions per episode depend on episode length and obstacle encounters and can be insensitive when agents avoid movement. Hyperparameter sensitivity: performance depends on tokenization parameters, SSM gating, and curriculum schedule, which may require extensive tuning.
